Item (1) — plan-version immutability lint (`workflow_lint.py`)
- Genuinely absent: zero occurrences of a plans-directory predicate in the lint

- **Committed-history baseline is CLEAN: 0 modify-after-add commits / 7277

  `.claude/worktrees/*` probed, no dirty plan files).
- **Load-bearing correction to the filing-time assumption:** the motivating
  #2061 v11 mutation NEVER LANDED IN COMMITTED HISTORY. `v11.md` shows one add
  (`eb53768bbd task #2061: plan v11`) followed only by pure `R100` renames
  through the status chain (terminal `dacf4e9371`), and it is byte-identical to
  its rename-resolved add commit. The mutation was working-tree-only and was
  reverted or superseded before any commit. **A history-only lint would
  therefore have been blind to the exact incident that motivated it** — the
  check must compare CURRENT (working-tree) content against the blob at the
  file's TRUE persist commit, not merely scan for committed `M` entries.
- Second correction: resolving the persist commit needs rename-FOLLOWING. A
  `--no-renames --diff-filter=A ... | tail -1` heuristic resolves #2061 v11 to
  the last status-move commit, not `eb53768bbd`, because `--no-renames` splits
  every folder move into D+A (this also explains why 306 paths appear to carry
  more than one add commit).

Item (2) — agent `model:` pin presence (`workflow_lint.py`)

- Corpus: all 43 repo agent files already carry a pin (`no_pin=0`), so a presence
  check is a zero-false-positive ratchet against the NEXT unpinned agent file
  rather than a fix for a live offender.
- The incident also cannot recur today for an unrelated reason:
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is set in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which sits at
  the TOP of the resolution chain and makes per-file pins inert while present.
- **Direct contradiction the plan must resolve, not paper over:** the existing
  function's docstring states that unpinned files are "silently skipped — agents
  may legitimately inherit their model from the parent (no pin = no runtime
  contract to validate)", and CLAUDE.md's "Prompt-cache key discipline" is cited

Item (3) — duplicate/conflicting GPU-hours token (`verify_plan.py`)
- Genuinely absent: `check_gpu_hours` (c5) parses with `GPU_LINE_RE.search(plan)`
  — FIRST match wins, no duplicate detection.
- **A naive "more than one token" FAIL is unshippable: 2468 / 3971 versioned plan
  files (62.2%) carry more than one token**, overwhelmingly legitimate repeats.
- Keying on DISTINCT values only still fails: all 11 files with conflicting raw
  values are FALSE POSITIVES of that predicate, in three shapes — a value quoted
  inside prose (#2177 v1 line 56), meta-discussion in a plan whose SUBJECT is
  this very checker (#625 v1-v3), and revision-history comparison tables
  (#524 v6/v7 line 19).
- **The correct predicate is a consumer/declaration MISMATCH, not a count.**
  Restricting to declaration-shaped tokens (line-anchored, optional bold or
  backtick wrap, nothing else on the line; fenced blocks stripped) and comparing
  against what the first-match consumer would read yields two clean arms:
  - ARM A, more than one distinct declaration-shaped value: **2 / 3971** files
    (#524 v2, v3 — both 590 vs 900).
  - ARM B, consumer first-match differs from the authoritative declaration:
    **5 / 3971 files (0.13%), zero false positives** — and ARM B CATCHES THE
    MOTIVATING INCIDENT: `tasks/awaiting_promotion/2061/plans/v7.md` and `v8.md`
    both read `consumer_first=70` against `decl=80`. The other three are
    #2177 v1 (consumer 65 vs declared 0 — the gate would size an autonomous
    auto-approve off a number quoted in prose), #524 v7 (400 vs 250) and
    #524 v6 (180 vs 400).
  - ARM B is the higher-value arm: the harm is the Step 2c gate consuming the
    WRONG estimate, which is exactly what a first-match parse in front of a
    prose-quoted or revision-table number produces.
- Constraint the plan must honor: 646 files carry a matching token but NO
  declaration-shaped token at all, so the check must never REQUIRE declaration
  shape — it compares only when one exists.
